text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn openly defended Istvan Nikolits, minister in charge with civil secret services saying his responsibility could only be raised in Operation Birch Tree if the minister had not taken any steps when he learned of the matter.

- Smallholders president Jozsef Torgyan yesterday said he will not recall deputy Speaker of Parliament Agnes G. Nagy Maczo from her post. Parliament's human rights committee accepted a proposal questioning Maczo's fitness for the post by a vote of 12-0, for four abstentions.
- Protesting farmers caused no chaos and little disruption in their efforts to tie up traffic yesterday.
- Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti yesterday outlined a draft report on planned changes to the armed forces as they prepare for NATO membership.

- Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene and Foreign Minister Erik Derycke told Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs in Brussels Wednesday that the EU should simultaneously meet all aspirants to EU membership in early 1998 for talks, and differentiation could only occur at a later stage.
- The Finno-Japanese consortium IVO-Tomen will purchase 73.76 percent of the power plant Budapesti Eromu Rt.
NEPSZABADSAG

- US Ambassador Donald Blinken said yesterday that while Hungary satisfies most of the principles determining the terms of NATO membership, it has a long way to go in achieving interoperability, i.e. co-operation with the North Atlantic Alliance.
- Socialist MP Laszlo Pal, board president of MOL yesterday announced that he will give up his parliamentary seat to satisfy the recently passed conflict of interest law.
- Hungarian and Austrian labour ministers signed two agreements in Szombathely yesterday.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Negotiations on the repayment of Russia of its remaining $500 million state debt to Hungary began in Budapest yesterday.
- Minister of Welfare Mihaly Kokeny and Romanian Health Minister Stefan Josif Dragulescu signed an agreement on co-operation in health and medical science.
- The secondary market of state securities reacted to the central bank's Monday interest rate hike with a quick yield increase.
- The Ministry of Industry will grant a HUF 487.5 million loan to the Eravis Hotel chain to finance the renovation and upgrading of its units.
- The April 28 AGM of Pick Rt. will vote on a plan to produce and sell mineral water found on company land.

- The parliamentary committee investigating the debt and bank consolidation programme said yesterday that the individual consolidation of specific banks such as Polgari Bank or Postabank is still a possibility.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The aim of the National Bank's 0.25 percent interest rate increase on Monday was to preserve the current level of forint savings, said Bank president Gyorgy Suranyi.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The National Bank of Hungary will register the forint rates of the Czech and Slovak koruna and the Polish zloty and abolish the publication of those of the Kuwaiti dinar and the Irish punt from April 1.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
